**Observation Log:**

- [FACT] The user is interested in learning more about the Amharic language.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Amharic is the official working language of Ethiopia, spoken by over 25 million people.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Amharic uses the Ge'ez or Ethiopic script, which consists of 33 basic letters and 7 modifications for vowel sounds.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Ge'ez script is written from left to right.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of Amharic letters include: አ (a), በ (b), ቺ (ch), ደ (d), ከ (k).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Amharic has a complex vowel system with 7 vowel sounds: አ (a), ኡ (u), ኢ (i), ኣ (ā), ኤ (e), ኦ (o), ኧ (ə).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Amharic has a Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) word order.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Verbs in Amharic agree with the subject in person, number, and gender, with three conjugations: present, past, and imperative.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Amharic has a complex system of tense and aspect with several forms to indicate different times and actions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The nominative-accusative case system in Amharic has two cases: nominative and accusative, with the accusative marked by the suffix -ን.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Possession in Amharic is indicated using possessive suffixes, such as አየ (my), አንቱ (your, singular), አታ (his/her/its).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Plurals in Amharic are formed using suffixes, such as አት (plural marker for nouns) and እን (plural marker for verbs).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Basic Amharic phrases include: ሰላም (Salam) - Hello, አደራሽ (Adersh) - Goodbye, አስተርአይ (Asterey) - Thank you, አይደል (Ayidel) - Yes, አይተን (Ayten) - No.
